metadata.title: Open Contracting Data Standard
metadata.version_line: Field Level Mapping Template - Version 0.9 - May 2022
instructions:
This mapping template is designed to support field-level mapping between your data sources and the 1.1 version of the Open Contracting Data Standard. A mapping template for version 1.0 of OCDS is available in the resources section of open-contracting.org.

A separate template for mapping codelists is available in the resources section of open-contracting.org.
Step 1:
Use the 1. Data Sources sheet to identify your sources of contracting data.

Step 2:
Populate the 2. Data elements sheet with a full list of data elements in your data sources. Where possible you should also provide examples for each data element.
Step 3:
Work through the (OCDS) sheets to identify the data available to publish at each stage of a contracting process. These sheets contain the available OCDS fields taken from the Schema sheets.
Note:
The following color coding is used throughout the mapping template:
White: Static data (column headings, examples, descriptions etc.)
Grey: Mapping guidance
Yellow: Data entry (manual input)
Purple: Calculated cell (do not edit)
Green: Lookup (select from list)
Red: Required field
Light grey: Objects that do not need mapping
More information

OCDS is designed to support real-time publication of events over the lifetime of a contracting process, from planning through to implementation. At each stage, new information can be provided, and earlier information repeated or updated. Each time information is provided, we call this an OCDS 'release'.
Multiple releases can be compiled together to provide a summary record of a contracting process.
Get support
Full documentation of the Open Contracting Data Standard is available at http://standard.open-contracting.org
A guidance for this mapping template is avaible at https://www.open-contracting.org/resources/ocds-1-1-mapping-template-guidance/
An overview of the mapping phase of OCDS implementation is available at https://standard.open-contracting.org/latest/en/guidance/map/#
You can also contact the OCP data team at data@open-contracting.org

general.title: Open Contracting Data Standard: General (all stages)
general.subtitle: Fields in this section apply at release level. Each release provides data about a single contracting process at a particular point in time. Releases can be used to notify users of new tenders, awards, contracts, and other updates.

tree.name: ocid
tree.title: Open Contracting ID
tree.description: A globally unique identifier for this Open Contracting Process. Composed of an ocid prefix and an identifier for the contracting process. For more information see the Open Contracting Identifier guidance

tree.name: id
tree.title: Release ID
tree.description: An identifier for this particular release of information. A release identifier must be unique within the scope of its related contracting process (defined by a common ocid). A release identifier must not contain the # character.

tree.name: date
tree.title: Release Date
tree.description: The date on which the information contained in the release was first recorded in, or published by, any system.

tree.name: tag
tree.title: Release Tag
tree.description: One or more values from the closed releaseTag codelist. Tags can be used to filter releases and to understand the kind of information that releases might contain.

tree.name: initiationType
tree.title: Initiation type
tree.description: The type of initiation process used for this contract, from the closed initiationType codelist.

tree.name: buyer
tree.title: Buyer
tree.description: A buyer is an entity whose budget will be used to pay for goods, works or services related to a contract. This may be different from the procuring entity who may be specified in the tender data.

children.name: name
children.title: Organization name
children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id
children.title: Organization ID
children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

tree.name: language
tree.title: Release language
tree.description: The default language of the data using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended.

tree.name: relatedProcesses
tree.title: Related processes
tree.description: The details of related processes: for example, if this process follows on from one or more other processes, represented under a separate open contracting identifier (ocid). This is commonly used to relate mini-competitions to their parent frameworks or individual tenders to a broader planning process.

children.name: id
children.title: Relationship ID
children.description: A local identifier for this relationship, unique within this array.

children.name: relationship
children.title: Relationship
children.description: The type of relationship, using the open relatedProcess codelist.

children.name: title
children.title: Related process title
children.description: The title of the related process, where referencing an open contracting process, this field should match the tender/title field in the related process.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The identification scheme used by this cross-reference, using the open relatedProcessScheme codelist.

children.name: identifier
children.title: Identifier
children.description: The identifier of the related process. If the scheme is 'ocid', this must be an Open Contracting ID (ocid).

children.name: uri
children.title: Related process URI
children.description: A URI pointing to a machine-readable document, release or record package containing the identified related process.

tree.title: Parties: Information on the parties (organizations, economic operators and other participants) who are involved in the contracting process and their roles, e.g. buyer, procuring entity, supplier etc. Organization references elsewhere in the schema are used to refer back to this entries in this list.

tree.name: buyer
tree.title: Buyer
tree.description: A buyer is an entity whose budget will be used to pay for goods, works or services related to a contract. This may be different from the procuring entity who may be specified in the tender data.

children.name: name
children.title: Common name
children.description: A common name for this organization or other participant in the contracting process. The identifier object provides a space for the formal legal name, and so this may either repeat that value, or may provide the common name by which this organization or entity is known. This field may also include details of the department or sub-unit involved in this contracting process.

children.name: id
children.title: Entity ID
children.description: The ID used for cross-referencing to this party from other sections of the release. This field may be built with the following structure {identifier.scheme}-{identifier.id}(-{department-identifier}).

children.name: identifier
children.title: Primary identifier
children.description: The primary identifier for this organization or participant. Identifiers that uniquely pick out a legal entity should be preferred. Consult the organization identifier guidance for the preferred scheme and identifier to use.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: Organization identifiers should be taken from an existing organization identifier list. The scheme field is used to indicate the list or register from which the identifier is taken. This value should be taken from the Organization Identifier Scheme codelist.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The identifier of the organization in the selected scheme.

children.name: legalName
children.title: Legal Name
children.description: The legally registered name of the organization.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to identify the organization, such as those provided by Open Corporates or some other relevant URI provider. This is not for listing the website of the organization: that can be done through the URL field of the Organization contact point.

children.name: additionalIdentifiers
children.title: Additional identifiers
children.description: A list of additional / supplemental identifiers for the organization or participant, using the organization identifier guidance. This can be used to provide an internally used identifier for this organization in addition to the primary legal entity identifier.

tree.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

tree.title: Process level title and description
tree.description: For providing overall process titles and descriptions, often to give a free-text summary of the contracting process as a whole.

tree.name: title
tree.title: Title
tree.description: A overall title for this contracting process or release.

tree.name: description
tree.title: Description
tree.description: An overall description of this contracting process or release. This does not replace a detailed breakdown of the objects of the contracting process in the planning, tender, award or contracts section.

tree.title: Bid statistics and details
tree.description: Allowing bid statistics, and detailed bid information to be represented.

tree.name: bids
tree.title: Bids
tree.description: The bid section is used to publish summary statistics, and where applicable, individual bid information.

children.name: statistics
children.title: Statistics
children.description: Summary statistics on the number and nature of bids received. Where information is provided on individual bids, these statistics should match those that can be calculated from the bid details array.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: An internal identifier for this statistic.

children.name: measure
children.title: Measure
children.description: The statistic reported in the value.

children.name: date
children.title: Date
children.description: The date when this statistic was last updated. This is often the closing date of the tender process. This field may be omitted unless either (a) the same statistic is provided from multiple points in time, or (b) there is a specific local requirement for the date when statistics were calculated to be provided.

children.name: value
children.title: Value
children.description: The value for the measure in question. Total counts should be provided as an integer. Percentages should be provided as a proportion of 1 (e.g. 10% = 0.1)

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount in the `value` field, if the statistic has a monetary value.

children.name: notes
children.title: Notes
children.description: Any notes needed to understand or interpret the given statistic.

children.name: relatedLot
children.title: Related Lot
children.description: Where lots are in use, if this statistic relates to bids on a particular lot, provide the lot identifier here. If left blank, the statistic will be interpreted as applying to the whole tender.

children.name: details
children.title: Bid details
children.description: An array of bids, providing information on the bidders, and where applicable, bid status, bid values and related documents. The extent to which this information can be disclosed varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local identifier for this bid

children.name: date
children.title: Date
children.description: The date when this bid was received.

children.name: status
children.title: Status
children.description: The status of the bid.

children.name: tenderers
children.title: Tenderer
children.description: The party, or parties, responsible for this bid.

children.name: name
children.title: Organization name
children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id
children.title: Organization ID
children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: value
children.title: Value
children.description: The total value of the bid.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: documents
children.title: Documents
children.description: All documents and attachments related to the bid and its evaluation.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: documentType
children.title: Document type
children.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: The document title.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

children.name: url
children.title: URL
children.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

children.name: datePublished
children.title: Date published
children.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

children.name: dateModified
children.title: Date modified
children.description: Date that the document was last modified

children.name: format
children.title: Format
children.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

children.name: language
children.title: Language
children.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

children.name: tenderers
children.title: Tenderer
children.description: The party, or parties, responsible for this bid.

children.title: Common name
children.description: A common name for this organization or other participant in the contracting process. The identifier object provides a space for the formal legal name, and so this may either repeat that value, or may provide the common name by which this organization or entity is known. This field may also include details of the department or sub-unit involved in this contracting process.

tree.title: Lots
tree.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this bid relates to one or more specific lots, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

tree.section: If you have additional information applicable at this level and not covered by the core OCDS schema or extensions, list the data items below, along with a proposed description. This information can be used to develop new OCDS extensions.

flat.name: ocid
flat.title: Open Contracting ID
flat.description: A globally unique identifier for this Open Contracting Process. Composed of an ocid prefix and an identifier for the contracting process. For more information see the Open Contracting Identifier guidance

flat.name: id
flat.title: Release ID
flat.description: An identifier for this particular release of information. A release identifier must be unique within the scope of its related contracting process (defined by a common ocid). A release identifier must not contain the # character.

flat.name: date
flat.title: Release Date
flat.description: The date on which the information contained in the release was first recorded in, or published by, any system.

flat.name: tag
flat.title: Release Tag
flat.description: One or more values from the closed releaseTag codelist. Tags can be used to filter releases and to understand the kind of information that releases might contain.

flat.name: initiationType
flat.title: Initiation type
flat.description: The type of initiation process used for this contract, from the closed initiationType codelist.

flat.name: buyer
flat.title: Buyer
flat.description: A buyer is an entity whose budget will be used to pay for goods, works or services related to a contract. This may be different from the procuring entity who may be specified in the tender data.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Organization name
flat.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Organization ID
flat.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: language
flat.title: Release language
flat.description: The default language of the data using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended.

flat.name: relatedProcesses
flat.title: Related processes
flat.description: The details of related processes: for example, if this process follows on from one or more other processes, represented under a separate open contracting identifier (ocid). This is commonly used to relate mini-competitions to their parent frameworks or individual tenders to a broader planning process.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Relationship ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this relationship, unique within this array.

flat.name: relationship
flat.title: Relationship
flat.description: The type of relationship, using the open relatedProcess codelist.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Related process title
flat.description: The title of the related process, where referencing an open contracting process, this field should match the tender/title field in the related process.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: The identification scheme used by this cross-reference, using the open relatedProcessScheme codelist.

flat.name: identifier
flat.title: Identifier
flat.description: The identifier of the related process. If the scheme is 'ocid', this must be an Open Contracting ID (ocid).

flat.name: uri
flat.title: Related process URI
flat.description: A URI pointing to a machine-readable document, release or record package containing the identified related process.

flat.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

flat.title: Process level title and description
flat.description: For providing overall process titles and descriptions, often to give a free-text summary of the contracting process as a whole.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: A overall title for this contracting process or release.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: An overall description of this contracting process or release. This does not replace a detailed breakdown of the objects of the contracting process in the planning, tender, award or contracts section.

flat.title: Bid statistics and details
flat.description: Allowing bid statistics, and detailed bid information to be represented.

flat.name: bids
flat.title: Bids
flat.description: The bid section is used to publish summary statistics, and where applicable, individual bid information.

flat.name: statistics
flat.title: Statistics
flat.description: Summary statistics on the number and nature of bids received. Where information is provided on individual bids, these statistics should match those that can be calculated from the bid details array.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: An internal identifier for this statistic.

flat.name: measure
flat.title: Measure
flat.description: The statistic reported in the value.

flat.name: date
flat.title: Date
flat.description: The date when this statistic was last updated. This is often the closing date of the tender process. This field may be omitted unless either (a) the same statistic is provided from multiple points in time, or (b) there is a specific local requirement for the date when statistics were calculated to be provided.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The value for the measure in question. Total counts should be provided as an integer. Percentages should be provided as a proportion of 1 (e.g. 10% = 0.1)

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount in the `value` field, if the statistic has a monetary value.

flat.name: notes
flat.title: Notes
flat.description: Any notes needed to understand or interpret the given statistic.

flat.name: relatedLot
flat.title: Related Lot
flat.description: Where lots are in use, if this statistic relates to bids on a particular lot, provide the lot identifier here. If left blank, the statistic will be interpreted as applying to the whole tender.

flat.name: details
flat.title: Bid details
flat.description: An array of bids, providing information on the bidders, and where applicable, bid status, bid values and related documents. The extent to which this information can be disclosed varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this bid

flat.name: date
flat.title: Date
flat.description: The date when this bid was received.

flat.name: status
flat.title: Status
flat.description: The status of the bid.

flat.name: tenderers
flat.title: Tenderer
flat.description: The party, or parties, responsible for this bid.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Organization name
flat.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Organization ID
flat.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The total value of the bid.

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: documents
flat.title: Documents
flat.description: All documents and attachments related to the bid and its evaluation.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: documentType
flat.title: Document type
flat.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: The document title.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

flat.name: url
flat.title: URL
flat.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

flat.name: datePublished
flat.title: Date published
flat.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

flat.name: dateModified
flat.title: Date modified
flat.description: Date that the document was last modified

flat.name: format
flat.title: Format
flat.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

flat.name: language
flat.title: Language
flat.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

flat.description: A list of additional / supplemental identifiers for the organization or participant, using the organization identifier guidance. This can be used to provide an internally used identifier for this organization in addition to the primary legal entity identifier.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: Organization identifiers should be taken from an existing organization identifier list. The scheme field is used to indicate the list or register from which the identifier is taken. This value should be taken from the Organization Identifier Scheme codelist.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: The identifier of the organization in the selected scheme.

flat.name: legalName
flat.title: Legal Name
flat.description: The legally registered name of the organization.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to identify the organization, such as those provided by Open Corporates or some other relevant URI provider. This is not for listing the website of the organization: that can be done through the URL field of the Organization contact point.

flat.name: address
flat.title: Address
flat.description: An address. This may be the legally registered address of the organization, or may be a correspondence address for this particular contracting process.

flat.name: streetAddress
flat.title: Street address
flat.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

flat.name: locality
flat.title: Locality
flat.description: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

flat.name: region
flat.title: Region
flat.description: The region. For example, CA.

flat.name: postalCode
flat.title: Postal code
flat.description: The postal code. For example, 94043.

flat.name: countryName
flat.title: Country name
flat.description: The country name. For example, United States.

flat.name: contactPoint
flat.title: Contact point
flat.description: Contact details that can be used for this party.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Name
flat.description: The name of the contact person, department, or contact point, for correspondence relating to this contracting process.

flat.name: email
flat.title: Email
flat.description: The e-mail address of the contact point/person.

flat.name: telephone
flat.title: Telephone
flat.description: The telephone number of the contact point/person. This should include the international dialing code.

flat.name: faxNumber
flat.title: Fax number
flat.description: The fax number of the contact point/person. This should include the international dialing code.

flat.name: url
flat.title: URL
flat.description: A web address for the contact point/person.

flat.name: roles
flat.title: Party roles
flat.description: The party's role(s) in the contracting process, using the open partyRole codelist.

flat.name: details
flat.title: Details
flat.description: Additional classification information about parties can be provided using partyDetail extensions that define particular fields and classification schemes.

flat.section: If you have additional information applicable at this level and not covered by the core OCDS schema or extensions, list the data items below, along with a proposed description. This information can be used to develop new OCDS extensions.

planning.title: Open Contracting Data Standard: Planning
planning.subtitle: Information from the planning phase of the contracting process. Note that many other fields can be filled in a planning release, in the appropriate fields in other schema sections; these would likely be estimates at this stage, e.g. value in tender.

tree.name: rationale
tree.title: Rationale
tree.description: The rationale for the procurement provided in free text. More detail can be provided in an attached document.

tree.name: budget
tree.title: Budget
tree.description: Details of the budget that funds this contracting process.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: An identifier for the budget line item which provides funds for this contracting process. This identifier should be possible to cross-reference against the provided data source.

children.name: description
children.title: Budget Source
children.description: A short free text description of the budget source. May be used to provide the title of the budget line, or the programme used to fund this project.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: The value reserved in the budget for this contracting process. A negative value indicates anticipated income to the budget as a result of this contracting process, rather than expenditure. Where the budget is drawn from multiple sources, the budget breakdown extension can be used.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: project
children.title: Project title
children.description: The name of the project through which this contracting process is funded (if applicable). Some organizations maintain a registry of projects, and the data should use the name by which the project is known in that registry. No translation option is offered for this string, as translated values can be provided in third-party data, linked from the data source above.

children.name: projectID
children.title: Project identifier
children.description: An external identifier for the project that this contracting process forms part of, or is funded via (if applicable). Some organizations maintain a registry of projects, and the data should use the identifier from the relevant registry of projects.

children.name: uri
children.title: Linked budget information
children.description: A URI pointing directly to a machine-readable record about the budget line-item or line-items that fund this contracting process. Information can be provided in a range of formats, including using IATI, the Open Fiscal Data Standard or any other standard which provides structured data on budget sources. Human readable documents can be included using the planning.documents block.

tree.name: documents
tree.title: Documents
tree.description: A list of documents related to the planning process.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: documentType
children.title: Document type
children.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: The document title.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

children.name: url
children.title: URL
children.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

children.name: datePublished
children.title: Date published
children.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

children.name: dateModified
children.title: Date modified
children.description: Date that the document was last modified

children.name: format
children.title: Format
children.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

children.name: language
children.title: Language
children.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

tree.name: milestones
tree.title: Planning milestones
tree.description: A list of milestones associated with the planning stage.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local identifier for this milestone, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a milestone through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: Milestone title

children.name: type
children.title: Milestone type
children.description: The nature of the milestone, using the open milestoneType codelist.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A description of the milestone.

children.name: code
children.title: Milestone code
children.description: Milestone codes can be used to track specific events that take place for a particular kind of contracting process. For example, a code of 'approvalLetter' can be used to allow applications to understand this milestone represents the date an approvalLetter is due or signed.

children.name: dueDate
children.title: Due date
children.description: The date the milestone is due.

children.name: dateMet
children.title: Date met
children.description: The date on which the milestone was met.

children.name: dateModified
children.title: Date modified
children.description: The date the milestone was last reviewed or modified and the status was altered or confirmed to still be correct.

children.name: status
children.title: Status
children.description: The status that was realized on the date provided in `dateModified`, from the closed milestoneStatus codelist.

tree.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

tree.title: Lots
tree.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this milestone relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

tender.title: Open Contracting Data Standard: Tender
tender.subtitle: Data regarding tender process - publicly inviting prospective contractors to submit bids for evaluation and selecting a winner or winners.

tree.name: id
tree.title: Tender ID
tree.description: An identifier for this tender process. This may be the same as the ocid, or may be an internal identifier for this tender.

tree.name: title
tree.title: Tender title
tree.description: A title for this tender. This will often be used by applications as a headline to attract interest, and to help analysts understand the nature of this procurement.

tree.name: description
tree.title: Tender description
tree.description: A summary description of the tender. This complements any structured information provided using the items array. Descriptions should be short and easy to read. Avoid using ALL CAPS.

tree.name: status
tree.title: Tender status
tree.description: The current status of the tender, from the closed tenderStatus codelist.

tree.name: procuringEntity
tree.title: Procuring entity
tree.description: The entity managing the procurement. This may be different from the buyer who pays for, or uses, the items being procured.

children.name: name
children.title: Organization name
children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id
children.title: Organization ID
children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

tree.name: items
tree.title: Items to be procured
tree.description: The goods and services to be purchased, broken into line items wherever possible. Items should not be duplicated, but the quantity specified instead.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local identifier to reference and merge the items by. Must be unique within a given array of items.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A description of the goods, services to be provided.

children.name: classification
children.title: Classification
children.description: The primary classification for the item.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

children.name: additionalClassifications
children.title: Additional classifications
children.description: An array of additional classifications for the item.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

children.name: quantity
children.title: Quantity
children.description: The number of units to be provided.

children.name: unit
children.title: Unit
children.description: A description of the unit in which the supplies, services or works are provided (e.g. hours, kilograms) and the unit-price.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The list from which identifiers for units of measure are taken, using the open unitClassificationScheme codelist. 'UNCEFACT' is recommended.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The identifier from the codelist referenced in the `scheme` field. Check the unitClassificationScheme codelist for details of how to find and use identifiers from the scheme in use.

children.name: name
children.title: Name
children.description: Name of the unit.

children.name: value
children.title: Value
children.description: The monetary value of a single unit.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: The machine-readable URI for the unit of measure, provided by the scheme.

tree.name: value
tree.title: Value
tree.description: The total upper estimated value of the procurement. A negative value indicates that the contracting process may involve payments from the supplier to the buyer (commonly used in concession contracts).

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

tree.name: minValue
tree.title: Minimum value
tree.description: The minimum estimated value of the procurement.  A negative value indicates that the contracting process may involve payments from the supplier to the buyer (commonly used in concession contracts).

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

tree.name: procurementMethod
tree.title: Procurement method
tree.description: The procurement method, from the closed method codelist.

tree.name: procurementMethodDetails
tree.title: Procurement method details
tree.description: Additional detail on the procurement method used. This field can be used to provide the local name of the particular procurement method used.

tree.name: procurementMethodRationale
tree.title: Procurement method rationale
tree.description: Rationale for the chosen procurement method. This is especially important to provide a justification in the case of limited tenders or direct awards.

tree.name: mainProcurementCategory
tree.title: Main procurement category
tree.description: The primary category describing the main object of this contracting process, from the closed procurementCategory codelist.

tree.name: additionalProcurementCategories
tree.title: Additional procurement categories
tree.description: Any additional categories describing the objects of this contracting process, using the open extendedProcurementCategory codelist.

tree.name: awardCriteria
tree.title: Award criteria
tree.description: The award criteria for the procurement, using the open awardCriteria codelist.

tree.name: awardCriteriaDetails
tree.title: Award criteria details
tree.description: Any detailed or further information on the award or selection criteria.

tree.name: submissionMethod
tree.title: Submission method
tree.description: The methods by which bids are submitted, using the open submissionMethod codelist.

tree.name: submissionMethodDetails
tree.title: Submission method details
tree.description: Any detailed or further information on the submission method. This can include the address, e-mail address or online service to which bids are submitted, and any special requirements to be followed for submissions.

tree.name: tenderPeriod
tree.title: Tender period
tree.description: The period when the tender is open for submissions. The end date is the closing date for tender submissions.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

children.name: endDate
children.title: End date
children.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

children.name: maxExtentDate
children.title: Maximum extent
children.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

children.name: durationInDays
children.title: Duration (days)
children.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

tree.name: enquiryPeriod
tree.title: Enquiry period
tree.description: The period during which potential bidders may submit questions and requests for clarification to the entity managing procurement. Details of how to submit enquiries should be provided in attached notices, or in submissionMethodDetails. Structured dates for when responses to questions will be made can be provided using tender milestones.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

children.name: endDate
children.title: End date
children.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

children.name: maxExtentDate
children.title: Maximum extent
children.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

children.name: durationInDays
children.title: Duration (days)
children.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

tree.name: hasEnquiries
tree.title: Has enquiries?
tree.description: A true/false field to indicate whether any enquiries were received during the tender process. Structured information on enquiries that were received, and responses to them, can be provided using the enquiries extension.

tree.name: eligibilityCriteria
tree.title: Eligibility criteria
tree.description: A description of any eligibility criteria for potential suppliers.

tree.name: awardPeriod
tree.title: Evaluation and award period
tree.description: The period for decision making regarding the contract award. The end date should be the date on which an award decision is due to be finalized. The start date may be used to indicate the start of an evaluation period.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

tree.name: contractPeriod
tree.title: Contract period
tree.description: The period over which the contract is estimated or required to be active. If the tender does not specify explicit dates, the duration field may be used.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

children.name: endDate
children.title: End date
children.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

tree.name: numberOfTenderers
tree.title: Number of tenderers
tree.description: The number of parties who submit a bid.

tree.name: tenderers
tree.title: Tenderers
tree.description: All parties who submit a bid on a tender. More detailed information on bids and the bidding organization can be provided using the bid extension.

children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id

children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.
