children.name: format
children.title: Format
children.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

children.name: language
children.title: Language
children.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

tree.name: milestones
tree.title: Milestones
tree.description: A list of milestones associated with the tender.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local identifier for this milestone, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a milestone through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: Milestone title

children.name: type
children.title: Milestone type
children.description: The nature of the milestone, using the open milestoneType codelist.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A description of the milestone.

children.name: code
children.title: Milestone code
children.description: Milestone codes can be used to track specific events that take place for a particular kind of contracting process. For example, a code of 'approvalLetter' can be used to allow applications to understand this milestone represents the date an approvalLetter is due or signed.

children.name: dueDate
children.title: Due date
children.description: The date the milestone is due.

children.name: dateMet
children.title: Date met
children.description: The date on which the milestone was met.

children.name: dateModified
children.title: Date modified
children.description: The date the milestone was last reviewed or modified and the status was altered or confirmed to still be correct.

children.name: status
children.title: Status
children.description: The status that was realized on the date provided in `dateModified`, from the closed milestoneStatus codelist.

tree.name: amendments
tree.title: Amendments
tree.description: A tender amendment is a formal change to the tender, and generally involves the publication of a new tender notice/release. The rationale and a description of the changes made can be provided here.

children.name: date
children.title: Amendment date
children.description: The date of this amendment.

children.name: rationale
children.title: Rationale
children.description: An explanation for the amendment.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: An identifier for this amendment: often the amendment number

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A free text, or semi-structured, description of the changes made in this amendment.

children.name: amendsReleaseID
children.title: Amended release (identifier)
children.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **before** the amendment was made.

children.name: releaseID
children.title: Amending release (identifier)
children.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **after** the amendment was made.

tree.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

tree.title: Lots
tree.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

children.name: relatedLot
children.title: Related lot
children.description: If this item belongs to a lot, provide the identifier of the related lot here.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: If this milestone relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

children.name: lots
children.title: Lots
children.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLots identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender. Properties of tender can be overridden for a given Lot through their inclusion in the Lot object.

children.name: id
children.title: Lot ID
children.description: A local identifier for this lot, such as a lot number. This is used in relatedLots references at the item, document and award level.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: A title for this lot.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A description of this lot.

children.name: status
children.title: Lot Status
children.description: The current status of the process related to this lot.

children.name: value
children.title: Lot value
children.description: The maximum estimated value of this lot.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: contractPeriod
children.title: Contract period
children.description: The period over which the contract is estimated or specified to be active. If the lot does not specify explicit dates, the duration field can be used.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

children.name: endDate
children.title: End date
children.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

children.name: maxExtentDate
children.title: Maximum extent
children.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

children.name: durationInDays
children.title: Duration (days)
children.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

children.name: lotDetails
children.title: Lot Details
children.description: If this tender is divided into lots, details can be provided here of any criteria that apply to bidding on these lots.

children.name: maximumLotsBidPerSupplier
children.title: Maximum lots per supplier
children.description: The maximum number of lots that one supplier can bid on as part of this contracting process.

children.name: maximumLotsAwardedPerSupplier
children.title: Maximum lots per supplier
children.description: The maximum number of lots that can be awarded to one supplier as part of this contracting process.

children.name: awardCriteriaDetails
children.title: Award criteria details
children.description: Any detailed or further information on the award or selection criteria.

children.name: lotGroups
children.title: Lot groups
children.description: Where the buyer reserves the right to combine lots, or wishes to specify the total value for a group of lots, a lot group is used to capture this information.

children.name: id
children.title: Lot group identifier
children.description: A local identifier for this group of lots.

children.name: relatedLots
children.title: Related lot(s)
children.description: A list of the identifiers of the lots that form this group. Lots can appear in more than one group.

children.name: optionToCombine
children.title: Option to combine
children.description: The buyer reserves the right to combine the lots in this group when awarding a contract.

children.name: maximumValue
children.title: Maximum value
children.description: The maximum estimated value of the lots in this group. This can be lower than the sum total of lot values

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

tree.title: Location
tree.description: Allows the point of delivery or site of works for a given line item to be indicated in tender, award and contract objects.

children.name: deliveryLocation
children.title: Delivery Location
children.description: The location where activity related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered, or will take place.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A name or description of this location. This might include the name(s) of the location(s), or might provide a human-readable description of the location to be covered.

children.name: geometry
children.title: Geometry
children.description: We follow the GeoJSON standard to express basic location information, using longitude, latitude, and optional elevation values in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection. A point location can be identified by geocoding a delivery address. For concession licenses, or other contracts covering a polygon location which is not contained in a known gazetteer, polygon and multi-polygon can be used.

children.name: type
children.title: Type
children.description: The type of GeoJSON Geometry Objects being provided. To provide longitude, latitude, and optional elevation, use 'Point', and enter an array of [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation] as the value of the coordinates field: e.g. [-122.085, 37.42].

children.name: coordinates
children.title: Coordinates
children.description: The relevant array of points, e.g. [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation], or a nested array of points, for the GeoJSON geometry being described. The longitude and latitude must be expressed in decimal degrees in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection.

children.name: gazetteer
children.title: Gazetteer
children.description: Identifiers from a gazetteer (a geographical index or directory) for the location.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Gazetteer scheme
children.description: The identifier of the gazetteer. The `locationGazetteers.csv` codelist provides details of services, where available, that can resolve a gazetteer entry to provide location names.

children.name: identifiers
children.title: Identifiers
children.description: An array of one or more codes drawn from the gazetteer indicated by the `scheme` field.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to a further description of the activity location. This might be a human-readable document with information on the location, or a machine-readable description of the location.

children.name: deliveryAddress
children.title: Delivery Address
children.description: The address to which, or where, goods or services related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered.

children.name: streetAddress
children.title: Street address
children.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

children.name: locality
children.title: Locality
children.description: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

children.name: region
children.title: Region
children.description: The region. For example, CA.

children.name: postalCode
children.title: Postal code
children.description: The postal code. For example, 94043.

children.name: countryName
children.title: Country name
children.description: The country name. For example, United States.

tree.title: Participation Fees
tree.description: Where a tender process involves payment of fees to access documents, submit a proposal, or be awarded a contract, this extension can be used to provide fee details.

children.name: participationFees
children.title: Participation fees
children.description: Any fees applicable to bidders wishing to participate in the tender process. Fees can apply for accessing bidding documents or for submitting bids, or there can be a "win fee" payable by the successful bidder.

children.name: id
children.title: Fee ID
children.description: A local identifier for this fee, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a fee through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: type
children.title: Fee type
children.description: The type of this fee.

children.name: value
children.title: Value
children.description: The monetary value of this fee.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: Additional information about this fee, for example: the specific cases in which the fee is applicable (e.g. hard copies of documents only), the way in which the fee is levied, or the exact nature of the fee.

children.name: methodOfPayment
children.title: Method(s) of payment
children.description: The accepted ways in which fees can be paid.

tree.title: Enquiries
tree.description: The enquiries extension can be used to record questions raised during a contracting process, and the answers provided.

children.name: enquiries
children.title: Enquiries
children.description: Questions sent to the procuring entity, and the answers given

children.name: id
children.title: Identifier
children.description: A unique identifier for the enquiry.

children.name: date
children.title: Date
children.description: The date the enquiry was received or processed.

children.name: author
children.title: Question author
children.description: The party asking this question. The corresponding entry in the `parties` array should have 'enquirer' in its `roles` array. Procurement policies vary on whether or not the identity of those asking questions is disclosed, or at which stage this information is disclosed.

children.name: name
children.title: Organization name
children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id
children.title: Organization ID
children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: title
children.title: Question title
children.description: The subject line of the question.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: The body of the question.

children.name: answer
children.title: Answer
children.description: The answer to this question, when available.

children.name: dateAnswered
children.title: Date answered
children.description: The date the answer to the question was provided.

children.name: relatedItem
children.title: Related item
children.description: If this question relates to a specific line-item, this field contains the line-item identifier.

children.name: relatedLot
children.title: Related lot
children.description: Where lots are used, if this question relates to a specific lot, this field contains the lot identifier.

children.name: threadID
children.title: Thread identifier
children.description: If this question and answer forms part of a discussion thread (e.g. the question is a follow-up to a previous answer) a thread identifier can be used to associate multiple enquiries.

tree.section: If you have additional information applicable at this level and not covered by the core OCDS schema or extensions, list the data items below, along with a proposed description. This information can be used to develop new OCDS extensions.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Tender ID
flat.description: An identifier for this tender process. This may be the same as the ocid, or may be an internal identifier for this tender.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Tender title
flat.description: A title for this tender. This will often be used by applications as a headline to attract interest, and to help analysts understand the nature of this procurement.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Tender description
flat.description: A summary description of the tender. This complements any structured information provided using the items array. Descriptions should be short and easy to read. Avoid using ALL CAPS.

flat.name: status
flat.title: Tender status
flat.description: The current status of the tender, from the closed tenderStatus codelist.

flat.name: procuringEntity
flat.title: Procuring entity
flat.description: The entity managing the procurement. This may be different from the buyer who pays for, or uses, the items being procured.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Organization name
flat.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Organization ID
flat.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: items
flat.title: Items to be procured
flat.description: The goods and services to be purchased, broken into line items wherever possible. Items should not be duplicated, but the quantity specified instead.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local identifier to reference and merge the items by. Must be unique within a given array of items.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A description of the goods, services to be provided.

flat.name: classification
flat.title: Classification
flat.description: The primary classification for the item.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

flat.name: additionalClassifications
flat.title: Additional classifications
flat.description: An array of additional classifications for the item.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

flat.name: quantity
flat.title: Quantity
flat.description: The number of units to be provided.

flat.name: unit
flat.title: Unit
flat.description: A description of the unit in which the supplies, services or works are provided (e.g. hours, kilograms) and the unit-price.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: The list from which identifiers for units of measure are taken, using the open unitClassificationScheme codelist. 'UNCEFACT' is recommended.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: The identifier from the codelist referenced in the `scheme` field. Check the unitClassificationScheme codelist for details of how to find and use identifiers from the scheme in use.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Name
flat.description: Name of the unit.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The monetary value of a single unit.

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: The machine-readable URI for the unit of measure, provided by the scheme.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The total upper estimated value of the procurement. A negative value indicates that the contracting process may involve payments from the supplier to the buyer (commonly used in concession contracts).

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: minValue
flat.title: Minimum value
flat.description: The minimum estimated value of the procurement.  A negative value indicates that the contracting process may involve payments from the supplier to the buyer (commonly used in concession contracts).

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: procurementMethod
flat.title: Procurement method
flat.description: The procurement method, from the closed method codelist.

flat.name: procurementMethodDetails
flat.title: Procurement method details
flat.description: Additional detail on the procurement method used. This field can be used to provide the local name of the particular procurement method used.

flat.name: procurementMethodRationale
flat.title: Procurement method rationale
flat.description: Rationale for the chosen procurement method. This is especially important to provide a justification in the case of limited tenders or direct awards.

flat.name: mainProcurementCategory
flat.title: Main procurement category
flat.description: The primary category describing the main object of this contracting process, from the closed procurementCategory codelist.

flat.name: additionalProcurementCategories
flat.title: Additional procurement categories
flat.description: Any additional categories describing the objects of this contracting process, using the open extendedProcurementCategory codelist.

flat.name: awardCriteria
flat.title: Award criteria
flat.description: The award criteria for the procurement, using the open awardCriteria codelist.

flat.name: awardCriteriaDetails
flat.title: Award criteria details
flat.description: Any detailed or further information on the award or selection criteria.

flat.name: submissionMethod
flat.title: Submission method
flat.description: The methods by which bids are submitted, using the open submissionMethod codelist.

flat.name: submissionMethodDetails
flat.title: Submission method details
flat.description: Any detailed or further information on the submission method. This can include the address, e-mail address or online service to which bids are submitted, and any special requirements to be followed for submissions.

flat.name: tenderPeriod
flat.title: Tender period
flat.description: The period when the tender is open for submissions. The end date is the closing date for tender submissions.

flat.name: startDate
flat.title: Start date
flat.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

flat.name: endDate
flat.title: End date
flat.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent
flat.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)
flat.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.name: enquiryPeriod
flat.title: Enquiry period
flat.description: The period during which potential bidders may submit questions and requests for clarification to the entity managing procurement. Details of how to submit enquiries should be provided in attached notices, or in submissionMethodDetails. Structured dates for when responses to questions will be made can be provided using tender milestones.

flat.name: startDate
flat.title: Start date
flat.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

flat.name: endDate
flat.title: End date
flat.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent
flat.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)
flat.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.name: hasEnquiries
flat.title: Has enquiries?
flat.description: A true/false field to indicate whether any enquiries were received during the tender process. Structured information on enquiries that were received, and responses to them, can be provided using the enquiries extension.

flat.name: eligibilityCriteria
flat.title: Eligibility criteria
flat.description: A description of any eligibility criteria for potential suppliers.

flat.name: awardPeriod
flat.title: Evaluation and award period
flat.description: The period for decision making regarding the contract award. The end date should be the date on which an award decision is due to be finalized. The start date may be used to indicate the start of an evaluation period.

flat.name: startDate
flat.title: Start date
flat.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

flat.name: endDate
flat.title: End date
flat.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent
flat.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)
flat.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.name: contractPeriod
flat.title: Contract period
flat.description: The period over which the contract is estimated or required to be active. If the tender does not specify explicit dates, the duration field may be used.

flat.name: startDate
flat.title: Start date
flat.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

flat.name: endDate
flat.title: End date
flat.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent
flat.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)
flat.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.name: numberOfTenderers
flat.title: Number of tenderers
flat.description: The number of parties who submit a bid.

flat.name: tenderers
flat.title: Tenderers
flat.description: All parties who submit a bid on a tender. More detailed information on bids and the bidding organization can be provided using the bid extension.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Organization name
flat.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Organization ID
flat.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: documents
flat.title: Documents
flat.description: All documents and attachments related to the tender, including any notices. See the documentType codelist for details of potential documents to include. Common documents include official legal notices of tender, technical specifications, evaluation criteria, and, as a tender process progresses, clarifications and replies to queries.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: documentType
flat.title: Document type
flat.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: The document title.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

flat.name: url
flat.title: URL
flat.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

flat.name: datePublished
flat.title: Date published
flat.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

flat.name: dateModified
flat.title: Date modified
flat.description: Date that the document was last modified

flat.name: format
flat.title: Format
flat.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

flat.name: language
flat.title: Language
flat.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

flat.name: milestones
flat.title: Milestones
flat.description: A list of milestones associated with the tender.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this milestone, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a milestone through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: Milestone title

flat.name: type
flat.title: Milestone type
flat.description: The nature of the milestone, using the open milestoneType codelist.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A description of the milestone.

flat.name: code
flat.title: Milestone code
flat.description: Milestone codes can be used to track specific events that take place for a particular kind of contracting process. For example, a code of 'approvalLetter' can be used to allow applications to understand this milestone represents the date an approvalLetter is due or signed.

flat.name: dueDate
flat.title: Due date
flat.description: The date the milestone is due.

flat.name: dateMet
flat.title: Date met
flat.description: The date on which the milestone was met.

flat.name: dateModified
flat.title: Date modified
flat.description: The date the milestone was last reviewed or modified and the status was altered or confirmed to still be correct.

flat.name: status
flat.title: Status
flat.description: The status that was realized on the date provided in `dateModified`, from the closed milestoneStatus codelist.

flat.name: amendments
flat.title: Amendments
flat.description: A tender amendment is a formal change to the tender, and generally involves the publication of a new tender notice/release. The rationale and a description of the changes made can be provided here.

flat.name: date
flat.title: Amendment date
flat.description: The date of this amendment.

flat.name: rationale
flat.title: Rationale
flat.description: An explanation for the amendment.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: An identifier for this amendment: often the amendment number

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A free text, or semi-structured, description of the changes made in this amendment.

flat.name: amendsReleaseID
flat.title: Amended release (identifier)
flat.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **before** the amendment was made.

flat.name: releaseID
flat.title: Amending release (identifier)
flat.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **after** the amendment was made.

flat.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

flat.title: Lots
flat.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

flat.name: relatedLot
flat.title: Related lot
flat.description: If this item belongs to a lot, provide the identifier of the related lot here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this milestone relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.name: lots
flat.title: Lots
flat.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLots identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender. Properties of tender can be overridden for a given Lot through their inclusion in the Lot object.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Lot ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this lot, such as a lot number. This is used in relatedLots references at the item, document and award level.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: A title for this lot.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A description of this lot.

flat.name: status
flat.title: Lot Status
flat.description: The current status of the process related to this lot.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Lot value
flat.description: The maximum estimated value of this lot.

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: contractPeriod
flat.title: Contract period
flat.description: The period over which the contract is estimated or specified to be active. If the lot does not specify explicit dates, the duration field can be used.

flat.name: startDate
flat.title: Start date
flat.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

flat.name: endDate
flat.title: End date
flat.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent
flat.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)
flat.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.name: lotDetails
flat.title: Lot Details
flat.description: If this tender is divided into lots, details can be provided here of any criteria that apply to bidding on these lots.

flat.name: maximumLotsBidPerSupplier
flat.title: Maximum lots per supplier
flat.description: The maximum number of lots that one supplier can bid on as part of this contracting process.

flat.name: maximumLotsAwardedPerSupplier
flat.title: Maximum lots per supplier
flat.description: The maximum number of lots that can be awarded to one supplier as part of this contracting process.

flat.name: awardCriteriaDetails
flat.title: Award criteria details
flat.description: Any detailed or further information on the award or selection criteria.

flat.name: lotGroups
flat.title: Lot groups
flat.description: Where the buyer reserves the right to combine lots, or wishes to specify the total value for a group of lots, a lot group is used to capture this information.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Lot group identifier
flat.description: A local identifier for this group of lots.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: A list of the identifiers of the lots that form this group. Lots can appear in more than one group.

flat.name: optionToCombine
flat.title: Option to combine
flat.description: The buyer reserves the right to combine the lots in this group when awarding a contract.

flat.name: maximumValue
flat.title: Maximum value
flat.description: The maximum estimated value of the lots in this group. This can be lower than the sum total of lot values

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.title: Location
flat.description: Allows the point of delivery or site of works for a given line item to be indicated in tender, award and contract objects.

flat.name: deliveryLocation
flat.title: Delivery Location
flat.description: The location where activity related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered, or will take place.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A name or description of this location. This might include the name(s) of the location(s), or might provide a human-readable description of the location to be covered.

flat.name: geometry
flat.title: Geometry
flat.description: We follow the GeoJSON standard to express basic location information, using longitude, latitude, and optional elevation values in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection. A point location can be identified by geocoding a delivery address. For concession licenses, or other contracts covering a polygon location which is not contained in a known gazetteer, polygon and multi-polygon can be used.

flat.name: type
flat.title: Type
flat.description: The type of GeoJSON Geometry Objects being provided. To provide longitude, latitude, and optional elevation, use 'Point', and enter an array of [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation] as the value of the coordinates field: e.g. [-122.085, 37.42].

flat.name: coordinates
flat.title: Coordinates
flat.description: The relevant array of points, e.g. [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation], or a nested array of points, for the GeoJSON geometry being described. The longitude and latitude must be expressed in decimal degrees in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection.

flat.name: gazetteer
flat.title: Gazetteer
flat.description: Identifiers from a gazetteer (a geographical index or directory) for the location.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Gazetteer scheme
flat.description: The identifier of the gazetteer. The `locationGazetteers.csv` codelist provides details of services, where available, that can resolve a gazetteer entry to provide location names.

flat.name: identifiers
flat.title: Identifiers
flat.description: An array of one or more codes drawn from the gazetteer indicated by the `scheme` field.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to a further description of the activity location. This might be a human-readable document with information on the location, or a machine-readable description of the location.

flat.name: deliveryAddress
flat.title: Delivery Address
flat.description: The address to which, or where, goods or services related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered.

flat.name: streetAddress
flat.title: Street address
flat.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

flat.name: locality
flat.title: Locality
flat.description: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

flat.name: region
flat.title: Region
flat.description: The region. For example, CA.

flat.name: postalCode
flat.title: Postal code
flat.description: The postal code. For example, 94043.

flat.name: countryName
flat.title: Country name
flat.description: The country name. For example, United States.

flat.title: Participation Fees
flat.description: Where a tender process involves payment of fees to access documents, submit a proposal, or be awarded a contract, this extension can be used to provide fee details.

flat.name: participationFees
flat.title: Participation fees
flat.description: Any fees applicable to bidders wishing to participate in the tender process. Fees can apply for accessing bidding documents or for submitting bids, or there can be a "win fee" payable by the successful bidder.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Fee ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this fee, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a fee through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: type
flat.title: Fee type
flat.description: The type of this fee.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The monetary value of this fee.

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: Additional information about this fee, for example: the specific cases in which the fee is applicable (e.g. hard copies of documents only), the way in which the fee is levied, or the exact nature of the fee.

flat.name: methodOfPayment
flat.title: Method(s) of payment
flat.description: The accepted ways in which fees can be paid.

flat.title: Enquiries
flat.description: The enquiries extension can be used to record questions raised during a contracting process, and the answers provided.

flat.name: enquiries
flat.title: Enquiries
flat.description: Questions sent to the procuring entity, and the answers given

flat.name: id
flat.title: Identifier
flat.description: A unique identifier for the enquiry.

flat.name: date
flat.title: Date
flat.description: The date the enquiry was received or processed.

flat.name: author
flat.title: Question author
flat.description: The party asking this question. The corresponding entry in the `parties` array should have 'enquirer' in its `roles` array. Procurement policies vary on whether or not the identity of those asking questions is disclosed, or at which stage this information is disclosed.

flat.name: name
flat.title: Organization name
flat.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Organization ID
flat.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Question title
flat.description: The subject line of the question.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: The body of the question.

flat.name: answer
flat.title: Answer
flat.description: The answer to this question, when available.

flat.name: dateAnswered
flat.title: Date answered
flat.description: The date the answer to the question was provided.

flat.name: relatedItem
flat.title: Related item
flat.description: If this question relates to a specific line-item, this field contains the line-item identifier.

flat.name: relatedLot
flat.title: Related lot
flat.description: Where lots are used, if this question relates to a specific lot, this field contains the lot identifier.

flat.name: threadID
flat.title: Thread identifier
flat.description: If this question and answer forms part of a discussion thread (e.g. the question is a follow-up to a previous answer) a thread identifier can be used to associate multiple enquiries.

flat.section: If you have additional information applicable at this level and not covered by the core OCDS schema or extensions, list the data items below, along with a proposed description. This information can be used to develop new OCDS extensions.

award.title: Open Contracting Data Standard: Awards
award.subtitle: Information from the award phase of the contracting process. There can be more than one award per contracting process e.g. because the contract is split among different providers, or because it is a standing offer.

tree.name: id
tree.title: Award ID
tree.description: The identifier for this award. It must be unique and must not change within the Open Contracting Process it is part of (defined by a single ocid). See the identifier guidance for further details.

tree.name: title
tree.title: Title
tree.description: Award title

tree.name: description
tree.title: Description
tree.description: Award description

tree.name: status
tree.title: Award status
tree.description: The current status of the award, from the closed awardStatus codelist.

tree.name: date
tree.title: Award date
tree.description: The date of the contract award. This is usually the date on which a decision to award was made.

tree.name: value
tree.title: Value
tree.description: The total value of this award. In the case of a framework contract this may be the total estimated lifetime value, or maximum value, of the agreement. There may be more than one award per procurement. A negative value indicates that the award may involve payments from the supplier to the buyer (commonly used in concession contracts).

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

tree.name: suppliers
tree.title: Suppliers
tree.description: The suppliers awarded this award. If different suppliers have been awarded different items or values, these should be split into separate award blocks.

children.name: name
children.title: Organization name
children.description: The name of the party being referenced. This must match the name of an entry in the parties section.

children.name: id
children.title: Organization ID
children.description: The id of the party being referenced. This must match the id of an entry in the parties section.

tree.name: items
tree.title: Items awarded
tree.description: The goods and services awarded in this award, broken into line items wherever possible. Items should not be duplicated, but the quantity specified instead.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local identifier to reference and merge the items by. Must be unique within a given array of items.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A description of the goods, services to be provided.

children.name: classification
children.title: Classification
children.description: The primary classification for the item.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

children.name: additionalClassifications
children.title: Additional classifications
children.description: An array of additional classifications for the item.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The scheme or codelist from which the classification code is taken. For line item classifications, this uses the open itemClassificationScheme codelist.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The classification code taken from the scheme.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A textual description or title for the classification code.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: A URI to uniquely identify the classification code.

children.name: quantity
children.title: Quantity
children.description: The number of units to be provided.

children.name: unit
children.title: Unit
children.description: A description of the unit in which the supplies, services or works are provided (e.g. hours, kilograms) and the unit-price.

children.name: scheme
children.title: Scheme
children.description: The list from which identifiers for units of measure are taken, using the open unitClassificationScheme codelist. 'UNCEFACT' is recommended.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: The identifier from the codelist referenced in the `scheme` field. Check the unitClassificationScheme codelist for details of how to find and use identifiers from the scheme in use.

children.name: name
children.title: Name
children.description: Name of the unit.

children.name: value
children.title: Value
children.description: The monetary value of a single unit.

children.name: amount
children.title: Amount
children.description: Amount as a number.

children.name: currency
children.title: Currency
children.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

children.name: uri
children.title: URI
children.description: The machine-readable URI for the unit of measure, provided by the scheme.

tree.name: contractPeriod
tree.title: Contract period
tree.description: The period for which the contract has been awarded.

children.name: startDate
children.title: Start date
children.description: The start date for the period. When known, a precise start date must be provided.

children.name: endDate
children.title: End date
children.description: The end date for the period. When known, a precise end date must be provided.

children.name: maxExtentDate
children.title: Maximum extent
children.description: The period cannot be extended beyond this date. This field can be used to express the maximum available date for extension or renewal of this period.

children.name: durationInDays
children.title: Duration (days)
children.description: The maximum duration of this period in days. A user interface can collect or display this data in months or years as appropriate, and then convert it into days when storing this field. This field can be used when exact dates are not known. If a startDate and endDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and endDate. Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

tree.name: documents
tree.title: Documents
tree.description: All documents and attachments related to the award, including any notices.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

children.name: documentType
children.title: Document type
children.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

children.name: title
children.title: Title
children.description: The document title.

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

children.name: url
children.title: URL
children.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

children.name: datePublished
children.title: Date published
children.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

children.name: dateModified
children.title: Date modified
children.description: Date that the document was last modified

children.name: format
children.title: Format
children.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

children.name: language
children.title: Language
children.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

tree.name: amendments
tree.title: Amendments
tree.description: An award amendment is a formal change to the details of the award, and generally involves the publication of a new award notice/release. The rationale and a description of the changes made can be provided here.

children.name: date
children.title: Amendment date
children.description: The date of this amendment.

children.name: rationale
children.title: Rationale
children.description: An explanation for the amendment.

children.name: id
children.title: ID
children.description: An identifier for this amendment: often the amendment number

children.name: description
children.title: Description
children.description: A free text, or semi-structured, description of the changes made in this amendment.

children.name: amendsReleaseID
children.title: Amended release (identifier)
children.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **before** the amendment was made.

children.name: releaseID
children.title: Amending release (identifier)
children.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **after** the amendment was made.

flat.name: endDate

flat.name: maxExtentDate
flat.title: Maximum extent

flat.name: durationInDays
flat.title: Duration (days)

Otherwise, if a startDate and maxExtentDate are set, this field, if used, should be equal to the difference between startDate and maxExtentDate.

flat.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

flat.title: Lots
flat.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

flat.name: relatedLot
flat.title: Related lot
flat.description: If this item belongs to a lot, provide the identifier of the related lot here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this award relates to one or more specific lots, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.title: Location
flat.description: Allows the point of delivery or site of works for a given line item to be indicated in tender, award and contract objects.

flat.name: deliveryLocation
flat.title: Delivery Location
flat.description: The location where activity related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered, or will take place.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A name or description of this location. This might include the name(s) of the location(s), or might provide a human-readable description of the location to be covered.

flat.name: geometry
flat.title: Geometry
flat.description: We follow the GeoJSON standard to express basic location information, using longitude, latitude, and optional elevation values in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection. A point location can be identified by geocoding a delivery address. For concession licenses, or other contracts covering a polygon location which is not contained in a known gazetteer, polygon and multi-polygon can be used.

flat.name: type
flat.title: Type
flat.description: The type of GeoJSON Geometry Objects being provided. To provide longitude, latitude, and optional elevation, use 'Point', and enter an array of [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation] as the value of the coordinates field: e.g. [-122.085, 37.42].

flat.name: coordinates
flat.title: Coordinates
flat.description: The relevant array of points, e.g. [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation], or a nested array of points, for the GeoJSON geometry being described. The longitude and latitude must be expressed in decimal degrees in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection.

flat.name: gazetteer
flat.title: Gazetteer
flat.description: Identifiers from a gazetteer (a geographical index or directory) for the location.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Gazetteer scheme
flat.description: The identifier of the gazetteer. The `locationGazetteers.csv` codelist provides details of services, where available, that can resolve a gazetteer entry to provide location names.

flat.name: identifiers
flat.title: Identifiers
flat.description: An array of one or more codes drawn from the gazetteer indicated by the `scheme` field.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to a further description of the activity location. This might be a human-readable document with information on the location, or a machine-readable description of the location.

flat.name: deliveryAddress
flat.title: Delivery Address
flat.description: The address to which, or where, goods or services related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered.

flat.name: streetAddress
flat.title: Street address
flat.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

flat.name: locality
flat.title: Locality
flat.description: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

flat.name: region
flat.title: Region
flat.description: The region. For example, CA.

flat.name: postalCode
flat.title: Postal code
flat.description: The postal code. For example, 94043.

flat.name: countryName
flat.title: Country name
flat.description: The country name. For example, United States.

flat.title: Bid statistics and details
flat.description: Allowing bid statistics, and detailed bid information to be represented.

flat.name: relatedBid
flat.title: Related bid
flat.description: Where bid details are used, a cross reference to the entry in the bids array to which this award relates. Provide the bid identifier here.

flat.name: value
flat.title: Value
flat.description: The monetary value of a single unit.

flat.name: amount
flat.title: Amount
flat.description: Amount as a number.

flat.name: currency
flat.title: Currency
flat.description: The currency of the amount, from the closed currency codelist.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: The machine-readable URI for the unit of measure, provided by the scheme.

flat.name: dateSigned
flat.title: Date signed
flat.description: The date the contract was signed. In the case of multiple signatures, the date of the last signature.

flat.name: documents
flat.title: Documents
flat.description: All documents and attachments related to the contract, including any notices.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local, unique identifier for this document. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a document through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: documentType
flat.title: Document type
flat.description: A classification of the document described, using the open documentType codelist.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: The document title.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A short description of the document. Descriptions are recommended to not exceed 250 words. In the event the document is not accessible online, the description field can be used to describe arrangements for obtaining a copy of the document.

flat.name: url
flat.title: URL
flat.description: A direct link to the document or attachment. The server providing access to this document ought to be configured to correctly report the document mime type.

flat.name: datePublished
flat.title: Date published
flat.description: The date on which the document was first published. This is particularly important for legally important documents such as notices of a tender.

flat.name: dateModified
flat.title: Date modified
flat.description: Date that the document was last modified

flat.name: format
flat.title: Format
flat.description: The format of the document, using the open IANA Media Types codelist (see the values in the 'Template' column), or using the 'offline/print' code if the described document is published offline. For example, web pages have a format of 'text/html'.

flat.name: language
flat.title: Language
flat.description: The language of the linked document using either two-letter ISO639-1, or extended BCP47 language tags. The use of lowercase two-letter codes from ISO639-1 is recommended unless there is a clear user need for distinguishing the language subtype.

flat.name: relatedProcesses
flat.title: Related processes
flat.description: The details of related processes: for example, if this process is followed by one or more contracting processes, represented under a separate open contracting identifier (ocid). This is commonly used to refer to subcontracts and to renewal or replacement processes for this contract.

flat.name: id
flat.title: Relationship ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this relationship, unique within this array.

flat.name: relationship
flat.title: Relationship
flat.description: The type of relationship, using the open relatedProcess codelist.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Related process title
flat.description: The title of the related process, where referencing an open contracting process, this field should match the tender/title field in the related process.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Scheme
flat.description: The identification scheme used by this cross-reference, using the open relatedProcessScheme codelist.

flat.name: identifier
flat.title: Identifier
flat.description: The identifier of the related process. If the scheme is 'ocid', this must be an Open Contracting ID (ocid).

flat.name: uri
flat.title: Related process URI
flat.description: A URI pointing to a machine-readable document, release or record package containing the identified related process.

flat.name: milestones
flat.title: Contract milestones
flat.description: A list of milestones associated with the finalization of this contract.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: A local identifier for this milestone, unique within this block. This field is used to keep track of multiple revisions of a milestone through the compilation from release to record mechanism.

flat.name: title
flat.title: Title
flat.description: Milestone title

flat.name: type
flat.title: Milestone type
flat.description: The nature of the milestone, using the open milestoneType codelist.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A description of the milestone.

flat.name: code
flat.title: Milestone code
flat.description: Milestone codes can be used to track specific events that take place for a particular kind of contracting process. For example, a code of 'approvalLetter' can be used to allow applications to understand this milestone represents the date an approvalLetter is due or signed.

flat.name: dueDate
flat.title: Due date
flat.description: The date the milestone is due.

flat.name: dateMet
flat.title: Date met
flat.description: The date on which the milestone was met.

flat.name: dateModified
flat.title: Date modified
flat.description: The date the milestone was last reviewed or modified and the status was altered or confirmed to still be correct.

flat.name: status
flat.title: Status
flat.description: The status that was realized on the date provided in `dateModified`, from the closed milestoneStatus codelist.

flat.name: amendments
flat.title: Amendments
flat.description: A contract amendment is a formal change to, or extension of, a contract, and generally involves the publication of a new contract notice/release, or some other documents detailing the change. The rationale and a description of the changes made can be provided here.

flat.name: date
flat.title: Amendment date
flat.description: The date of this amendment.

flat.name: rationale
flat.title: Rationale
flat.description: An explanation for the amendment.

flat.name: id
flat.title: ID
flat.description: An identifier for this amendment: often the amendment number

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A free text, or semi-structured, description of the changes made in this amendment.

flat.name: amendsReleaseID
flat.title: Amended release (identifier)
flat.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **before** the amendment was made.

flat.name: releaseID
flat.title: Amending release (identifier)
flat.description: Provide the identifier (release.id) of the OCDS release (from this contracting process) that provides the values for this contracting process **after** the amendment was made.

flat.section: Extensions are additions to the core OCDS schema which allow publishers to include extra information in their OCDS data. The following extensions are available for the present section:

flat.title: Lots
flat.description: A tender process can be divided into lots, where bidders can bid on one or more lots. Details of each lot can be provided here. Items, documents and other features may then reference the lot they are related to using relatedLot. Where no relatedLot identifier is given, the values ought to be interpreted as applicable to the whole tender.

flat.name: relatedLot
flat.title: Related lot
flat.description: If this item belongs to a lot, provide the identifier of the related lot here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this document relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.name: relatedLots
flat.title: Related lot(s)
flat.description: If this milestone relates to a particular lot, provide the identifier(s) of the related lot(s) here.

flat.title: Location
flat.description: Allows the point of delivery or site of works for a given line item to be indicated in tender, award and contract objects.

flat.name: deliveryLocation
flat.title: Delivery Location
flat.description: The location where activity related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered, or will take place.

flat.name: description
flat.title: Description
flat.description: A name or description of this location. This might include the name(s) of the location(s), or might provide a human-readable description of the location to be covered.

flat.name: geometry
flat.title: Geometry
flat.description: We follow the GeoJSON standard to express basic location information, using longitude, latitude, and optional elevation values in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection. A point location can be identified by geocoding a delivery address. For concession licenses, or other contracts covering a polygon location which is not contained in a known gazetteer, polygon and multi-polygon can be used.

flat.name: type
flat.title: Type
flat.description: The type of GeoJSON Geometry Objects being provided. To provide longitude, latitude, and optional elevation, use 'Point', and enter an array of [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation] as the value of the coordinates field: e.g. [-122.085, 37.42].

flat.name: coordinates
flat.title: Coordinates
flat.description: The relevant array of points, e.g. [longitude, latitude] or [longitude, latitude, elevation], or a nested array of points, for the GeoJSON geometry being described. The longitude and latitude must be expressed in decimal degrees in the WGS84 (EPSG:4326) projection.

flat.name: gazetteer
flat.title: Gazetteer
flat.description: Identifiers from a gazetteer (a geographical index or directory) for the location.

flat.name: scheme
flat.title: Gazetteer scheme
flat.description: The identifier of the gazetteer. The `locationGazetteers.csv` codelist provides details of services, where available, that can resolve a gazetteer entry to provide location names.

flat.name: identifiers
flat.title: Identifiers
flat.description: An array of one or more codes drawn from the gazetteer indicated by the `scheme` field.

flat.name: uri
flat.title: URI
flat.description: A URI to a further description of the activity location. This might be a human-readable document with information on the location, or a machine-readable description of the location.

flat.name: deliveryAddress
flat.title: Delivery Address
flat.description: The address to which, or where, goods or services related to this tender, contract or license will be delivered.

flat.name: streetAddress
flat.title: Street address
flat.description: The street address. For example, 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy.

flat.name: locality
flat.title: Locality
flat.description: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

flat.name: region
flat.title: Region
flat.description: The region. For example, CA.

flat.name: postalCode
flat.title: Postal code
flat.description: The postal code. For example, 94043.

flat.name: countryName
flat.title: Country name
flat.description: The country name. For example, United States.
